paper_metadata.title: ANALYSIS OF HESSIAN SCALING FOR LOCAL AND GLOBAL COSTS IN VARIATIONAL QUANTUM ALGORITHMS

summary: This paper analyzes Hessian-entry variance in variational quantum algorithms using exact second-order parameter-shift identities. For global objectives, it proves exponential decay of Varρ(Hjk) with system size n under a concentration assumption, while for term-wise local objectives in bounded-depth circuits it derives a polynomial bound Varρ(Hjk) ≤ cloc(k,r,L)VG(k+2rL)/n; numerically, the paper reports fits such as exp(-0.57 n), exp(-0.64 n), n^-1.96, n^-2.05, and TFIM VQE fits exp(-0.63 n) and n^-2.2.

experiments.description: Numerical study of Hessian-entry variance scaling for a hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit under a global cost function and a local averaged cost function, including finite-shot estimation effects.

algorithm.variant: hardware-efficient variational quantum algorithm for Hessian-scaling analysis
algorithm.ansatz: layered hardware-efficient ansatz with nearest-neighbor brickwork CNOT entanglers and single-qubit Ry rotations
algorithm.optimizer: SGD and quantum natural gradient (used only in finite-shot trajectory illustration)

hyperparameters.initializations_per_configuration: 200 i.i.d. initializations per (n, L) for scaling experiments; 150 random initializations for TFIM VQE benchmark
objective_types: TFIM VQE local energy density Clocal = <HTFIM>/(2n)
hyperparameters.measurement_backend: exact statevector backend for intrinsic variance experiments

algorithm.parameter_initialization: i.i.d. uniform random parameters; stated as U([-pi, pi)) equivalent to U([0, 2pi)) up to a global shift

problem_formulation.encoding_details: not an optimization-encoding study; qubits represent the variational state of an n-qubit circuit, with local observables acting on subsets of qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: C(theta) = <psi(theta)| O |psi(theta)>; specific objectives include Cglobal = <Z^{⊗n}> and Clocal = (1/n) sum_i <Z_i>; TFIM VQE uses Clocal = <HTFIM>/(2n) with HTFIM = -J sum_i Z_i Z_{i+1} - h sum_i X_i, J = h = 1
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: HTFIM = -J sum_i Z_i Z_{i+1} - h sum_i X_i (periodic boundary conditions, J = h = 1)

problem_instance.description: Synthetic scaling study plus a VQE benchmark on the 1D transverse-field Ising model under periodic boundary conditions

dataset_specification.description: periodic boundary conditions; critical point J = h = 1

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Empirical variances computed over random initializations; scaling fits via least squares on log scale (exponential) and log-log scale (power law); 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for variance estimates; 150 random initializations for TFIM benchmark; 200 initializations per (n, L) for main scaling plots

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Empirical variance estimation from repeated random initializations; least-squares fitting of exponential and power-law scaling; bootstrap confidence intervals; finite-shot variance decomposed into intrinsic initialization variance plus shot-noise term

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: finite-shot optimization trajectories shown for SGD and QNG; global objective nearly flat, local objective decreases more visibly

speedup_claims.factor: exponential shot-cost scaling for global objectives; polynomial shot-cost scaling for local objectives
speedup_claims.baseline_method: finite-shot Hessian-entry estimation via parameter-shift on a classical simulator / measurement process
speedup_claims.conditions: global objectives satisfying second-moment concentration; local term-wise objectives in bounded-depth circuits with sub-extensive backward lightcones
speedup_claims.caveats: This is not a computational speedup over a classical algorithm; it is a scaling claim about resolvability / measurement cost for Hessian entries.

speedup_claims.factor: O(1) shifted circuit evaluations per Hessian entry
speedup_claims.conditions: exact second-order parameter-shift identities with two-point-spectrum generators
speedup_claims.caveats: Constant-factor overhead only; does not imply overall efficiency for large n because shot requirements may still scale exponentially.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Entry-wise Hessian estimation via parameter-shift uses O(1) shifted circuit evaluations per Hessian entry; resolution shot cost scales exponentially for global objectives and polynomially for local objectives under sub-extensive lightcones

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No quantum advantage claim or classical-vs-quantum performance comparison; the paper studies variance scaling of Hessian entries in noiseless simulation and finite-shot estimation cost.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated speedup over classical methods
Focus is on theoretical scaling of Hessian variance and shot complexity
Finite-shot costs grow exponentially for global objectives and polynomially for local objectives, but this is not an advantage claim

notes: The paper reports only simulator-based numerical experiments using PennyLane with an exact statevector backend; no real QPU hardware is used.
SGD and QNG appear only as classical optimization baselines/illustrative trajectories, not separate quantum algorithms.
No transpilation, gate counts, or device fidelities are reported.
The paper reports only simulator-based numerical experiments and theoretical variance bounds.
SGD and QNG are used as illustrative optimization baselines, not as evidence of quantum advantage.
